object_description: Transparent low building volume opening toward an urban edge
design_condition: The building opens toward the northwest and is set low into the terrain, creating a public-facing edge and a level transition but extending into the protected garden and weakening its relationship with the principal outdoor space.

positive.statement: The transparent facade communicates a high level of publicity, which is rated positively.
The tree population is preserved and sensitively supplemented where the existing terrain remains unchanged.
The proposal meets the requirements of the desired sports operation.
The direct arrangement of equipment and technical rooms in the sports halls demonstrates a consistent and logical structure.
The cross-laminated timber ceilings are a sensible choice because they are easy to dismantle and reusable.

negative.statement: The orientation gives greater weight to the street than to the common listed outdoor space and neighboring building.
The two entrances obscure the formation of a clear address.
The building is set too low and extends into the listed garden, making its handling of the terrain and existing buildings critical.
The high traffic areas are rated negatively, and the complex surrounding access area produces interior spaces without natural daylight and ventilation.
Only one access would make operational access control easier for the various users.
The spatial proportions of the multifunctional rooms are not ideal for their users.
The beams penetrating the building envelope are questionable in a temporary building because of their complexity, sustainability, and economy.
The fire-protection measures required by the structural system appear questionable and require extensive cladding of the access zone.
The building is not very space efficient, has high resource use, and cannot achieve the required energy standard in its current form.
The large-format glazing causes significant summer heat input, while the absence of photovoltaic panels is a further weakness.
